surfaces.part: upper step riser / cliff wall band

answer.evidence: The tile is a full-width 48 px strip with no silhouette change. Rows 0-2 are a dark outline and a light lip, rows 3-14 are a darker, mottled vertical-looking band (cliff or riser), and row 15 is a dark 1-row line. Rows 16-29 are a lighter, flat, speckled surface, which is the tread seen from above. Rows 16-17 are a light edge band and rows 30-31 are a dark shadow band. There is no side face. Because it is a terrain tile, the dark band above the lighter surface reads as a descent seen from above. The geometry is ambiguous, so this is neither a standing 3/4 object nor a pure flat slab.

styleAnswer.evidence: The measured facts are fine: 7 visible tones per tile (the paving reference also has 7), 2% near-flat coverage, and 0% neutral dark edges, so the outlines lean brown rather than black. The grain is sparse, with no per-stone or per-tread shading like the paving's individually shaded cobbles or the grass's clumps and tufts. The whole piece uses only 7 colours, so each band looks smooth and sticker-like next to the reference. The tinted outline is correct, but the shading depth and texture density fall short of the reference quality bar.
